title: fix(superheroes): a PR-body finding is fixed in a staged copy and published by the review
body:
Closes #2083.

## What's changing, and why

When a review finds a problem in the PR body itself, the fix now goes into a copy of the body kept inside the review. An independent auditor checks it there. Once the loop ends converged, the review copies the audited text onto the PR and records that it did. Fixers are told never to write to GitHub at all. If the live body changed during the review, from a fixer's stray edit or anyone else's, the review refuses to overwrite it, and the record says so.

The reason for the change: before this, such a finding was either dropped or fixed by a fixer editing the live PR outside the review's record. That is what happened in a consuming project's PR.

## What we're accepting

- **Three small review findings are left for your ruling** (all Minor). I recommend you rule as follows:
  1. *"Publish reads GitHub even when there is no PR-body fix."* I recommend **keep as built**. That read is the only way the record catches a fixer that wrote the live body directly, which is the consuming-project case. A narrower wording nit, that a failed read says "did not copy its PR-body fix" when there was none, is follow-up FU2.
  2. *"The retry test can pass without proving the first publish time is kept."* It is real but test-only. I recommend **follow-up FU1**, not another review cycle.
  3. *"Distinguish the two publication timestamps."* This is the same point, carried from the first review session. I recommend you **rule it together with 2**.
- **A fixer running on codex or cursor cannot edit the staged copy.** Those engines' sandboxes only grant the worktree. Such a fixer reports a refused write and the finding goes unfixed, rather than reaching for GitHub. The default fixer (sandboxed claude) is granted the copy's directory.
- **Two GitHub writes a fixer could still make are not caught.**
  - A comment or review posted by a fixer outside the sandbox: the record only catches writes that change the PR body.
  - A sandboxed claude fixer is network-blocked, so its write attempts surface as recorded refusals.
  - Extending enforcement to unsandboxed fixers is follow-up FU3 (owner-call).
- **The change is bigger than estimated:** 440 non-test lines against a 185 estimate. The advisor ruled continue with one trim (480 → 439) and accepted the result.

## How to see it

N/A: say it. This changes a rule the review loop follows and has no screen to look at.

## Advisor vet

<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: READY** · 2aef058caa8c368b735b5673bd6bf5253abd53da

**What was checked.** Your "105 a". When a review finds a problem in the PR description, the fixer now fixes a copy kept inside the review. An auditor checks it there, and only once the review has finished cleanly does the review copy the result onto the PR. Fixers are told never to write to GitHub. I tried seven situations against the copy step:
- a checked fix copies across once;
- an unchecked fix, an unfinished review, or a description someone else edited meanwhile is refused;
- a fixer that edits the live description directly, the consuming project's case, now shows up in the record;
- a retry doesn't copy twice.

CI is green, and the second review session settled in one round.

**What accepting it means.** Fixes to PR descriptions go through the review's record instead of being dropped or written behind its back. Fixers on Codex or Cursor can't edit the copy, so their fix to a description goes unfixed rather than being made outside the record. A fixer that posts a stray comment instead of editing the description isn't detected; item 113 asks whether to build that. The change is about 440 lines. That's bigger than estimated; I ruled it continue after a trim.

**What is yours to decide.** None on the merge itself. I decided the reviewers' three small points as craft, and they're on the sheet under "decided for you". Items 113 and 114 are separate.

Receipt: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2086#issuecomment-6356997049

**Carried forward 2026-10-23 (merge train):** the head moved from `7ea8846` to `2aef058` by a plain `--no-ff` merge of `main` (`9d6fddf`, with #2078, #2080 and the #2070 stack). Two conflicts, both kept on both sides: the upgrade-notes list, and `lib/review_record_session.py`, where this PR and the #2070 stack each append one line to the review record's `checked` list (this PR's PR-body line, then main's verify-via line). This PR's own changed lines are identical (blank lines aside); 1037 tests covering `review_record_session`, `pr_body_stage` and the verify-via lines passed on the merge. The sheet is not republished (owner waiver, option d); CI runs on the new commit before the merge.

<!-- superheroes:build-record -->
<details><summary>Build record</summary>

**Lane:** full, declared with `build_lane.py declare`. The route is build-ready, on the owner's "105 a, file and launch".
**Anchor:** a ruling ([collector record](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/695#issuecomment-6355369120)). It resolved at intake.
**Brief:** [the brief](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2083#issuecomment-6355487595), amended in place after the brief-check. [Brief-check dispositions](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2083#issuecomment-6355578437): 4 Important and 1 Minor, all folded; F2 was folded in part and in part disputed (now FU3).
**Preflight:**
- `preflight_probe.py run` is go: gh auth, codex READY, dispatch-vocab.
- The real `gh` write was the [intake comment](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2083#issuecomment-6355434411).
- Browser probe: N/A (plugin build, no running app).
**Test-pilot:** N/A (no running app). The stand-ins are the receipts below and the two review sessions.

### What was built
- New `lib/pr_body_stage.py`, the one chokepoint that writes a PR body:
  - `stage` copies `pr.json`'s body to `pr-body/original.md` and `pr-body/staged.md`, once each.
  - The fixer's editable copy is `round-N/landing/dispatch-fixer/_pr-body.md`. That is the directory `dispatch-write --landing-dir` already grants to restricted claude file tools, and the reserved `_` prefix keeps the landing sweep from counting it as a stray.
  - `publish` copies the staged body onto the PR only after a converged terminal, only for the staged bytes an audit cleared, and never over a live body that moved since staging. It writes `pr-body/published.json` for every outcome, refusals included.
- `lib/round_driver.py`:
  - A finding cited at `SUPERHEROES_PR_BODY.md` passes compile's diff scope.
  - The fixer and audit orders gain a `PR_BODY_LINE` input.
  - The fixer fold copies the fixer's copy back and records its sha256.
  - The audit fold records `prBodyAudited` only when every audit target of the round cleared.
- `rubric/orders/dispatch-fixer.md` says the staged copy is the only place to fix a PR-body finding, and forbids every GitHub write. `dispatch-audits.md` says to read a PR-body fix in the staged copy.
- `review_record_session.py` adds one plain line to the record's `checked` list from `published.json`.
- Docs: `SKILL.md` gained one sentence (run `publish` before the record, on a converged terminal), `round-driver.md` gained `## PR-body findings`, and TRANSITION gained an Unreleased entry.

### Review
- **Session 1** ([record](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2086#issuecomment-6356708590)), at `559f8c041`:
  - Panel: codex `gpt-6.1-sol` @ xhigh on code-reviewer and test-role.
  - Round 1 fixed the one Important (`5aa0fe700`). The audit, codex and independent, discharged it.
  - The round-2 verify gate failed on `test_ssot_drift.py::test_round_driver_and_review_base_guard_raw_mode_read_census` (1 failed, 7467 passed), so the session **halted** honestly.
  - WO-3 (`7ea8846a9`) routed the new mode read through the census's existing spelling. No behaviour changed.
- **Session 2** ([record](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2086#issuecomment-6356941909)), at `7ea8846a9`:
  - The full panel ran again from round 1 and the session **converged**: `full-panel-confirmed`, independence `independent`, base fetched.
  - There was no blocking finding. Three Minors are left for the owner, listed above.
  - The record's status reads "not reviewed" only because those three await your ruling. CI on `7ea8846` is green ([run 39895766634](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/actions/runs/39895766634)).
- The grounding seat did not run. No loop phase runs it, and both records say so.
- Focus: the advisor asked the panel to check each of `publish`'s steps against the DoD. Session 1 reported the recovery step as unrequested, and the fix narrowed it to "a prior success receipt exists". Session 2 raised the remaining steps as Nits, and its verifiers refuted all three.

| Session | Finding | Sev | Verdict | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | test_pr_body_stage.py:399 Require refusal when matching live text has no recorded copy | Important | CONFIRMED | **fixed** `5aa0fe700` (adoption needs a prior success receipt; otherwise `pr-body-moved`), audit discharged |
| 1 | pr_body_stage.py:287 Remove the unrequested publication recovery protocol | Minor | PLAUSIBLE | narrowed by the same fix: receipt-free adoption removed, receipt-backed idempotence kept (a second publish must not overwrite its own success receipt) |
| 1 | test_pr_body_stage.py:392 Distinguish the two publication timestamps | Minor | CONFIRMED | **left for the owner**: recommend FU1 |
| 1 | pr_body_stage.py:271 Remove eligibility checks already enforced by the caller | Nit | REFUTED | dropped by verification |
| 1 | pr_body_stage.py:301 Remove the additional readback gate | Minor | REFUTED | dropped by verification |
| 1 | test_pr_body_stage.py:382 Remove the extra post-copy readback contract | Minor | REFUTED | dropped by verification |
| 2 | pr_body_stage.py:280 Return unchanged before querying GitHub | Minor | CONFIRMED | **left for the owner**, builder disputes: the live read is what catches a fixer's direct body write (the DoD's "a fixer that writes anyway is a refusal the record shows"); wording nit → FU2 |
| 2 | test_pr_body_stage.py:392 Retry test can pass without preserving the publication time | Minor | CONFIRMED | **left for the owner**: recommend FU1 |
| 2 | pr_body_stage.py:274 Remove the duplicate convergence gate | Nit | REFUTED | dropped by verification |
| 2 | pr_body_stage.py:287 Remove the speculative repeat-publish branch | Nit | REFUTED | dropped by verification |
| 2 | pr_body_stage.py:301 Remove the unrequested read-back phase | Nit | REFUTED | dropped by verification |

### Receipts (re-run by the orchestrator)
- **Scoped suite on `559f8c041`:** 424 passed (the eight order-related test files).
- **WO-3 on `7ea8846a9`:** `test_ssot_drift.py` + `test_pr_body_stage.py` passed, 183 tests.
- **Session 1's verify gate** ran the calibrated command, including `verify_touched_tests` over the 186 touched-test files, on `5aa0fe700`: 1 failed, 7467 passed (the census). WO-3 fixed that failure.
- **CI on `7ea8846a9`:** green, which covers the full suite on the final head.
- **Validators on `559f8c041`:** all five passed (pin, marketplace, hosts, skills, stubs).
- **Not run:** I did not run the local full suite. CI is the receipt.

### Bite-proofs
Declared set G1–G9, re-run by the orchestrator on `559f8c041` after the trim. WO-1's implementer recorded the same set on `903955f18`. Each line gives the neutralization, then the test that went red. Every element went red under its neutralization, and went green after the inverse edit restored it with `git status --porcelain` empty.

- G1, `_diff_scope_ok` citation exemption: `CITATION` → `CITATION + "#neutralized"`. Red: `test_a_finding_citing_the_pr_body_passes_compile_against_a_diff_that_does_not_hold_it`.
- G2, the fixer-order GitHub prohibition: "Never write to GitHub" → "Writing to GitHub is allowed". Red: `test_the_fixer_order_names_the_staged_copy_and_forbids_writing_to_github[host-seat]`. Disclosed by the implementer: the staged-copy-line half of G2 has no separate red.
- G3, the audit-order PR-body line: `- PR body:` → `- Staged:`. Red: `test_the_audit_order_names_the_staged_copy_and_the_original[host-seat]`.
- G4, `pr-body-not-audited`: prefix `False and`. Red: `test_E10_a_staged_body_that_is_not_the_audited_one_is_refused[none-recorded]`.
- G5, `pr-body-moved`: prefix `False and`. Red: `test_E11_a_live_body_that_moved_since_the_original_is_never_overwritten`.
- G6, `already-published`: prefix `False and`. Red: `test_E14_a_second_publish_after_success_edits_nothing_and_keeps_the_first_time`.
- G7, the audit fold's all-cleared condition: conjuncts → `True`. Red: `test_E10_the_audit_fold_records_nothing_unless_every_target_cleared[one-not-discharged]`.
- G8, the fixer fold's collect call: → `None`. Red: `test_the_fixer_fold_collects_the_fixer_copy_and_records_the_after_sha`.
- G9, `record_line` in the account: prefix `False and`. Red: `test_the_review_account_carries_the_publish_line`.

Accepted disclosure: G2's line half has no separate red. The same test asserts the staged-copy line, but removing the prohibition alone was the neutralization.

The orchestrator committed the trim (`559f8c041`, named in the commit body) and ran the tests and all bite-proofs itself |

Command refusals the implementers reported:
- WO-1: two compound commands were held by the harness. The implementer re-issued them split up, and disclosed that this is a retry in another form.
- WO-2: three commands were held or refused. After the third, the implementer stopped rather than retrying.

### Size tripwire
Crossed at `903955f18`: 480 non-test lines against the 185 estimate, a tripwire of 370. I messaged the advisor at 02:32 UTC. The advisor ruled continue with a trim ([size report](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2083#issuecomment-6355983553), [trim result](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2083#issuecomment-6356237549)) and then accepted 439 against the 350 aim. Final count 440 (bar 439) at `7ea8846a9`. The 300 bar was reported on the issue. Deleted files: none.

### DoD
<!-- superheroes:dod-table -->
| DoD bullet | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A PR-body finding runs end to end in a test: the fixer edits the staged copy, the audit reads it, the review copies it to the PR; the fixer order and audit order name the file | done | `test_pr_body_stage.py::test_a_pr_body_finding_is_fixed_audited_and_published_through_the_chokepoint` drives the real `mechanical_compile`, the rendered fixer and audit orders, the real `_fold_fixer`/`_fold_audits`, and `publish` with a fake `gh` |
| A test that a fixer order forbids GitHub writes | done | `test_the_fixer_order_names_the_staged_copy_and_forbids_writing_to_github[host-seat / engine-seat]` (bite-proof G2) |
| A consuming project's PR shape (three answer lines in the body) is the test fixture | done | `test_pr_body_stage.py` `BODY`/`FIXED`: a `## Test answers` heading with three answer lines, which the fix rewrites |
| TRANSITION notes it under `## Unreleased` | done | `TRANSITION.md`: a Before-you-upgrade bullet and `### Review: a PR-body finding is fixed in a staged copy` |

### Follow-ups for the advisor
Follow-ups: 5 (1 owner-call)
- FU1 [craft] Pin the retry test's timestamp. `test_E14…` runs two publishes in the same second, so it can't tell kept from re-stamped. Stub `PBS._now` to two different times (session-2 Minor, and session-1's "distinguish the two publication timestamps").
- FU2 [craft] `record_line` says "did not copy its PR-body fix" after `pr-body-live-unreadable` even when there was no fix. Word it as "could not check the PR body on GitHub" when staged equals original.
- FU3 [owner-call] Role-scoped GitHub-write enforcement for unsandboxed fixers, and detection of comment or review writes. This is the disputed half of brief-check F2, a new mechanism beyond #2083's scope.
- FU4 [info] The census `test_ssot_drift.py::…raw_mode_read_census` guards `round_driver.py` but sat outside WO-1's scoped test budget. The review's verify gate caught it. Orders that touch `round_driver.py` should name `test_ssot_drift.py` in their scoped budget.
- FU5 [defect] `repo_doctor.py` reports "verify command no longer resolves: if" for this repo's calibrated verify command, which begins with `if [ -x scripts/pinned-python ]`. It is a staleness false positive; the nudge printed on every review-code setup this build.
